articles.title: JPEG XL vs AVIF for web use-cases
articles.summary: JPEG XL vs AVIF for web use-cases has now landed in all major browsers, and its performance varies depending on the use-case. At default effort settings, AVIF almost always produces smaller files than JPEG XL, but at maximum effort settings, the gap narrows to typically 6-20%. The JPEG XL encoder matters a lot, especially for lossy photos, and its performance is generally better than AVIF. AVIF is faster to encode and decode, and uses less memory, but its files are typically larger, and its performance is better on balance.

A federated relay implementation, incorporating the Noise Protocol, will provide E2EE, preventing man-in-the-middle and replay attacks. This development is crucial for the OCapN group, enabling peer-to-peer applications to communicate securely in hostile environments.

A small number of sites sent headers aimed at AI systems, but most of these were pranks, and only a few asked for real actions. The majority of AI-directed headers were used to redirect agents to new resources, and some sites used headers to push back on agents, warning them away or telling them to follow the site's directions.

The problem is caused by a two-zero byte in sysfs, which is a file system view of the device's hardware. To fix the issue, the author had to write a kernel exploit for their own access point, which is a technical feat that requires knowledge of Linux and kernel development. The author notes that TP-Link's shell won't allow them to write these two zeros, so they had to write a kernel exploit to access the sysfs file.
